subject.title: [Mac App] node.invoke system.run causes WebSocket disconnection on macOS

question: Should maintainers require a live signed macOS companion-app reproduction before queueing a code repair for this `system.run` disconnect?
rationale: Source confirms the relevant current path, but the report is timing/network/runtime dependent and automation cannot safely choose between the Swift shell executor, shared node session, channel keepalive, or gateway pending-invoke layers without current-main device logs.

options.title: Run live diagnostics first
options.body: Pair a signed current-main macOS app to a gateway, run the reported `sleep 0.3 && echo ok` command, and collect correlated app and gateway logs before assigning a repair.

options.title: Use the broader flapping track
options.body: Treat this as partial overlap with the broader macOS node flapping issue, but keep this issue open until that path proves this specific `system.run` disconnect fixed.

options.title: Queue a source-led repair now
options.body: Let automation attempt a narrow Swift/gateway fix from source inspection alone, accepting a higher chance of touching the wrong layer.

recommendation.title: Run live diagnostics first
recommendation.body: Pair a signed current-main macOS app to a gateway, run the reported `sleep 0.3 && echo ok` command, and collect correlated app and gateway logs before assigning a repair.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current routing signal is prior macOS shell execution and node identity work near the reported path.
